CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue and CatalogDBInitializer.GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence cast the Int64 value returned by a SQL sequence to int without a range check. Values beyond Int32 range can wrap/truncate and produce invalid or duplicate identifiers.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types

CweFindings.Description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.
CweFindings.Explanation: Default.aspx.cs accepts the route size as pageSize and passes it through. PaginatedItemsViewModel divides count by pageSize without validating that it is nonzero; a size of zero causes an unhandled divide-by-zero exception while building the response.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Calculation

CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: ImageAzureStorage.UpLoadImageFromFile opens a FileStream with File.OpenRead and passes it to UploadFromStream, but does not dispose or close the stream after the upload, leaving the file handle open.
CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime

CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: ImageAzureStorage.UpLoadImageFromFile opens a FileStream with File.OpenRead and passes it to UploadFromStream, but does not dispose or close the stream after the upload, leaving the file handle open.
CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime

CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. The singleton owns a mutable List<CatalogItem> that request handlers enumerate and mutate without a lock, allowing concurrent web requests to race.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context

CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. The singleton owns a mutable List<CatalogItem> that request handlers enumerate and mutate without a lock, allowing concurrent web requests to race.
CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context

CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. The singleton owns a mutable List<CatalogItem> that request handlers enumerate and mutate without a lock, allowing concurrent web requests to race.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization

CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton. The singleton owns a mutable List<CatalogItem> that request handlers enumerate and mutate without a lock, allowing concurrent web requests to race.
CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization

CweFindings.Description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Compose configuration embeds the SQL Server administrator password in the database container environment and health-check command. The credential value is intentionally omitted from this assessment output.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Password

CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Explanation: ImageAzureStorage.InitializeCatalogImages assigns blob-level public read access to the pics container. UploadTempImage stores temporary user uploads in that same container, so temporary objects are also readable without application authentication.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Create_Click, Save_Click, and Delete_Click mutation handlers do not emit audit events, and the OIDC AuthenticationFailed callback redirects without logging the failure. Page-load messages do not record the security-relevant outcome or changed item.
CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging

CweFindings.Description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Compose configuration embeds a SQL Server administrator credential for the database container and its health check. The credential value is intentionally omitted from this assessment output.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: Catalog item Name and Description values are accepted from form input and persisted by CatalogService. Details.aspx and Delete.aspx render stored values with asp:Label Text data bindings rather than an HTML-encoding binding, allowing stored markup to be emitted as executable page content.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: PicUploader passes an uploaded file to ImageAzureStorage.UploadTempImage, which builds the blob object identifier from the caller-controlled file.FileName without normalizing path separators. The container is fixed, but the client can influence the object key and path segments within that storage container.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
